title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the 1975-76 notes on the divided-power De Rham complex. It is a typed typescript page headed '- 167 -' and 'IX', filed in the folder as archive page 485 (pencil '98'). Its content and numbering (13.1.1)-(13.1.3) fit SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie', Grothendieck, 1967-69, published 1972). That exposé has a final section on the transcendental (complex-analytic) case. The neighbouring pages, handwritten notes on simplicial flat modules and divided powers, are unrelated, so this is a stray sheet, possibly reused or misfiled.

The mathematics: S is a complex analytic space and A → S a smooth relative analytic group. Set E = Lie(A/S) = e^*(T_{A/S}), the pullback of the relative tangent sheaf along the zero section. It is locally free, and E denotes the corresponding analytic vector bundle.

The exponential exp: E → A is constructed in two steps:
- Near the zero section, use the formal-group exponential, which exists in characteristic 0 (the inverse of the logarithm), with analytic convergence.
- Extend to all of E by exp(x) = exp(x/n)^n.

exp is a homomorphism of relative analytic groups. It is étale, because its differential along the zero section is the identity and it is a homomorphism. Its image is the open subspace A^o, the union of the neutral components of the fibres. This gives an exact sequence 0 → R → E → A^o → 0, where R = ker(exp) is a relative analytic group étale over S (fibrewise a lattice-like discrete subgroup). R is closed in E if and only if A^o is separated over S, i.e. the zero section of A^o is closed. This is used later in SGA 7 IX to describe monodromy and the uniformization A^o = E/R of degenerating families of tori or abelian varieties over a punctured disc.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence 'R closed ⇔ zero section of A^o closed' holds because E → A^o is surjective and étale, hence open and a topological quotient map, and R is the preimage of the zero section. 'Prolongement par multiplicativité' implicitly requires checking analyticity and well-definedness in families. This is standard and locally fine.
Contextual: the page is misplaced relative to the folder's subject (divided-power De Rham complex). It is a typescript page of SGA 7 IX, not part of the manuscript notes.

transcription_corrections: The page header '- 167 -' and 'IX' indicates SGA 7 I, Exposé IX typescript pagination, not the manuscript's own numbering.
'A^o' denotes A with superscript zero (neutral component), sometimes written A^0.
